beat_player.text: Well fought, {player}. You will get your ground back, but not today, and I will remember the flank.
You held the ford better than I expected, {player}. Come find me in Calvenza and I will show you where the road should have gone.
That was a fair field, Ser {player}. Keep your {gold} for the levy next season, you will need it more than I will.
You fought hard, Ser {player}. Next time keep your reserve behind the hedge line, it saved me more than once in the first war.
{player} took a fine hill today. I have seen veterans fold on it, so take the praise and keep your temper steady.

beat_by_player.text: Ser {player} ran me down fair and square at the ridge. I lost {troop_count} men to it and I still sleep well tonight.
Good work on the ridge, {player}. You read my line better than most who have tried it. I will teach you the hedges sometime.
You have a sharp eye, Ser {player}. I gave up the field because the ground was yours, though I suspect you outthought me too.
Lost the field to {player} and I will not pretend it did not sting. The lesson is patience, so back to the drawing board I go.
{player}, you won that day but do not think the causeway is yours yet. I have a long memory and a shorter temper than you think.

fought_alongside_player.text: {player} held the left flank beside us against {enemy_faction} and never once broke rank. That is how the first war was won, really.
Thank you for the flank today, {player}. We would not have held the bridge without those {troop_count} spearmen you brought.
Stand where you are, Ser {player}, and we will hold these {enemy_faction} lines together. Keep your eyes on the ridge, not the dust.
Good ground held against {enemy_faction} today. Nobody went home without a story, and {player} can count that as a win.
Ser {player}, I would fight beside you again without needing a map. Let us get the wounded to the wagons before the rain comes.

released_by_player.text: You let me walk free instead of asking for gold, {player}. I will not forget that kindness, and the road to Calvenza is open to you.
{player} let the captives go without ransom today. Not many lords would bother with that, and I think it was the better choice.
Released without ransom, {player}. You made your point, and it cost you gold you could have used. We are square, mostly.
Thank you to {player} for the release. Ormerath has enough feuds, and it is good to see one ended without a village burning.

player_joined_my_faction.text: Welcome to {my_faction}, {player}. Ask me for a road map any time, and I will mark you the safest path to the fens.
{player} has sworn to {my_faction}. Good, the banner needed a steady hand, and this one looks like it means it.
So you have joined {my_faction}, {player}. Keep your head down in the council halls and you will be fine, or so I hope.
{player} now rides under {my_faction}. I will hold my tongue, but I have seen oaths broken before, so prove it on the field.
{player}, you took the oath to {my_faction} quickly. I hope the banner does not regret it, and neither do I, yet.

player_granted_fief.text: The lords have given {fief} to {player}. A fine choice, and I expect the fields will be better kept for it. Good luck, Ser.
So {fief} went to {player}. I would have liked a word with the council first, but I suppose the decision is theirs.
{fief} to {player}? I have held that ground longer than most of the council has been alive. Let us see how well it is kept.
Congratulations on {fief}, {player}. Walk the walls yourself the first week. Lords who do rarely lose their towns.
{fief} passed to {player} today. The people there will judge the grant by the harvest, not by the seal.

encounter_greeting.text: Ser {player}, {persona} of {my_faction} here. Our roads meet often enough, so tell me what you need and I will point you on.
Ser {player}, I am {persona} of {my_faction}. Mind the mud past the ford, it has swallowed better horses than yours.
Ser {player}. {persona} of {my_faction}. Your banners are on my road, but I am in no hurry to make a quarrel of it today.
Well met on the road, Ser {player}. {persona} of {my_faction} at your service, and the water here is good if your horses are thirsty.
Ser {player}, it is {persona} of {my_faction}. Let us both keep our swords sheathed and our wagons moving, shall we?

encounter_farewell.text: Safe travels, Ser {player}. The fens are kind in the morning, so keep to the causeway and you will be home by supper.
Farewell, Ser {player}. Keep your flank tight on the eastern road and you should miss the worst of the bandits.
Farewell, Ser {player}. Do not let the road make you hasty. We will meet again, and I would rather it be over a table.
Go well, Ser {player}. Let the horses drink at the next inn, and take the old causeway, it is shorter than the map suggests.
Until the next crossing, Ser {player}. Do not let the rain catch you in the reeds, the mud there is no friend to anyone.

ambient_chatter.text: Has anyone come up from {town} lately? The mill there is running again and the bread is finally decent, I am told.
The fog over {village} came in early this morning. Keep your lanterns lit on the marsh road if you are heading out.
Rain on the eastern road again. I remember when that stretch was only mud and reed, before anyone thought to lay stone.
Anyone bound for {town} should bring spare shoes for the horses. The smithy there is slow and the road is rough.
Quiet night in {village}. I am drawing the old road maps again for the new lords, so ask if you need one.

player_big_defeat.text: {player} lost {troop_count} men on the south road today. Hard loss, but the ones who come back stronger always have the best stories.
Ser {player}, I heard about the {troop_count} you lost. Come by when you are ready and I will share what I wish someone had told me.
A bad day for {player}, losing {troop_count} men like that. The road does not care who you are, only how you prepare for it.
{player} ran into a wall and lost {troop_count} men. Maybe scouts first next time, instead of charging the hedges head down.
You took a heavy blow, {player}. Losing {troop_count} men is no small thing. Rebuild quietly, and do not let the taverns make you rash.
